## Problem

This problem extends LeetCode 1242, Web Crawler Multithreaded; solving that earlier problem first is recommended.

Design a concurrent web crawler that receives a starting URL `startUrl` and an `HtmlParser`, and returns every distinct reachable URL whose hostname is exactly identical to the hostname of `startUrl`.

The crawler must obey these rules:

* Begin visiting from `startUrl`.
* A URL may be recorded and expanded only if its hostname exactly matches the hostname of `startUrl`. All URLs use `http` and do not contain a port.
* For any URL, the hostname is the portion between `"://"` and the next `'/'`, or the remainder of the string if no `'/'` appears.
* Before any hostname comparison or duplicate check, remove the fragment by deleting `'#'` and everything after it. If two URLs become equal after this normalization, they are considered the same URL. For example, `"http://example.com/page#section1"` and `"http://example.com/page"` both normalize to `"http://example.com/page"`.
* A normalized URL must be crawled and stored at most once.
* The hyperlink graph may contain cycles, and a page may link back to a previously seen page.

The following parser implementation is provided:

```java
/*
 * The parser is provided; do not modify it.
 */
class HtmlParser {
    // Returns the raw URLs found on the page identified by url.
    List<String> getUrls(String url) { ... }
}
```

Each `getUrls` call includes simulated network latency, so your solution must fetch multiple pages concurrently.

For testing, `urls`, `edges`, and `startUrl` describe the underlying graph. Your code may access only `startUrl`; `urls` and `edges` are not directly available.

Return all discovered URLs after sanitization, in any order.

Example 1:

```text
Input:
urls = ["http://example.com/page1", "http://example.com/page2", "http://example.com/page3#sectionA", "http://example.net/page4#"]
edges = [[0, 1], [0, 2], [1, 3], [2, 0]]
startUrl = "http://example.com/page1"

Output:
["http://example.com/page1", "http://example.com/page2", "http://example.com/page3"]
```

Explanation:
* All three reachable pages share the hostname "example.com".
* The URL "http://example.com/page3#sectionA" is sanitized to "http://example.com/page3".
* The page "http://example.net/page4#" is ignored due to a different hostname.

Example 2:

```text
Input:
urls = ["http://news.yahoo.com/home", "http://news.google.com/top", "http://news.yahoo.com/news"]
edges = [[1, 0], [0, 2]]
startUrl = "http://news.google.com/top"

Output:
["http://news.google.com/top"]
```

Example 3:

```text
Input:
urls = ["http://site.com/a", "http://site.com/b#frag1", "http://site.com/b#frag2", "http://site.com/c", "http://other.com/x", "http://site.com/d", "http://site.com/e#", "http://site.com/f"]
edges = [[0, 1], [0, 2], [1, 3], [2, 3], [3, 4], [3, 5], [5, 0], [5, 6], [6, 7], [7, 0]]
startUrl = "http://site.com/a"

Output:
["http://site.com/a", "http://site.com/b", "http://site.com/c", "http://site.com/d", "http://site.com/e", "http://site.com/f"]
```

Constraints:

* All URLs use the `http` protocol and do not contain a port number.
* 1 ≤ `urls.length` ≤ 1000,
* 1 ≤ `edges.length` ≤ 1000
* Each `getUrls` call will return in ≤ 15 ms.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Separate the concerns: one part extracts and compares hostnames, another part coordinates concurrent visits, and a third tracks which URLs are already seen.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a thread-safe set for visited URLs and a thread pool or worker queue to expand URLs in parallel without duplicating work.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The trickiest part is avoiding duplicate crawling and ensuring the hostname comparison is exact, including the scheme and no-port assumption.

</details>
